metadata.blueprint_markdown:
# Blueprint — Remix Inference Plus

## Current game reality

The working clone currently contains a single-page canvas arcade game in `index.html`. The implementation presents a meme/trash-panda feed-defense shooter: the player character sits near the bottom of the screen, follows horizontal mouse/touch dragging, automatically fires upward, and tries to destroy descending cleanup-tool enemies before they collide with the player.

### High-level code structure

- Inline CSS defines responsive full-screen canvas layout, mobile-safe overlay panels, HUD cards, hearts, buttons, damage flash, and GIF feedback wrappers.
- Inline JavaScript initializes an `AudioController`, canvas sizing, input listeners, game state, enemy/projectile/particle arrays, update logic, canvas rendering, and UI button bindings.
- The game is self-contained in `index.html`; no external local JS/CSS files are required for the core loop.

### Game loop / state model

1. Start panel is visible.
2. Start button primes audio, hides start panel, shows HUD, sets `gameActive = true`, calls `initGame()`, then starts `requestAnimationFrame(gameLoop)`.
3. Each active frame increments `frame`, spawns enemies by score-scaled frame interval, updates player/projectiles/enemies/particles/collisions, and redraws the canvas.
4. Enemy collision with the player removes one heart and triggers damage feedback.
5. Zero health stops BGM, shows game-over panel, and displays final score.
6. Restart button reinitializes state and re-enters the same loop.

### Player goals

- Survive the endless wave as long as possible.
- Defeat enemies for score.
- Avoid losing all three hearts.

### Interaction pattern

The implemented interaction is horizontal drag/move only. Shooting is automatic. There is no flap, jump, tap impulse, gravity arc, or pipe-gap navigation mechanic.

### Core systems

- Responsive full-window canvas.
- Mouse/touch horizontal input.
- Automatic projectile cadence.
- Score-scaled enemy spawning and speed.
- Three enemy archetypes: low-HP broom, tougher vacuum, weaving spray.
- AABB collision for projectile/enemy and enemy/player contact.
- Score HUD and heart health strip.
- Audio feedback, particles, screen shake, damage flash, and GIF overlays.

### Inferred genre/gameplay shape

This is a simple one-screen vertical arcade shooter / avoidance game with endless score-chase progression and mobile-first drag controls.

## Intended remixed trajectory

The user remix prompt is `flappy bird`. The safe interpretation is not to convert the game into a true Flappy Bird clone, because that would require changing protected input, physics, level layout, collision expectations, and moment-to-moment goals. Instead, downstream stages should transform the presentation into a flappy-sky arcade world:

> A scrappy bird/trash-panda courier glides through a vertical sky-feed route, auto-launching glowing feathers to stop pipe-like cleanup tools, vacuum drones, and crosswind sprays from sanitizing the feed.

## Preserve-vs-change guidance

### Preserve

- Horizontal drag control.
- Automatic shooting.
- Player anchored near the bottom.
- Enemy descent, optional weave, HP, score values, and contact damage semantics.
- Three-heart game-over flow.
- Existing start/play/game-over/restart state model.
- Canvas rendering architecture and mobile touch reliability.

### Change safely

- Title, copy, HUD labels, and button language.
- Player/enemy/background silhouettes.
- Color palette and procedural sky/pipes/clouds/feathers motifs.
- Particles and nonblocking visual feedback.
- Conceptual five-level world framing.
- Audio/GIF selections only through approved catalog remote URLs if media changes are needed.

## Downstream priority

1. First make the current loop read as a flappy-sky courier game through procedural art and copy.
2. Then create a level/world progression plan using visual evolution and existing pressure knobs.
3. Keep readability and mobile control safety above all theme ambitions.

The current workspace contains a single-file Three.js mobile arcade game titled **Easy Taxi 3D: Magic GPS / Sky Cab Dispatch Run**. - `index.html` contains all HTML, CSS, and game JavaScript.

# Remix v4 Blueprint — Flappy Fashion Aviary

## Current game reality

The current `index.html` implements **Style Shuffle Studio**, a single-file HTML5 styling toy. It is not mechanically a Flappy Bird clone or an avoidance game. The experience is built from:

- A full-window `<canvas>` render loop.
- A `START` overlay that transitions into `PLAY`.
- A centered animated character drawn procedurally on canvas.
- DOM button controls for toggling four outfit parts: top, bottom, shoes, and bow.
- A Quick Mix button that randomizes outfit colors and restores all pieces on.
- Cosmetic particles, feedback text, GIF reactions, and audio cues.
- A mobile-first bottom controls panel.

There is no scoring, level system, pipe collision, gravity/flap physics, hazard avoidance, death state, round timer, collectible economy, or win condition.

## High-level code structure

- **HTML/CSS shell:** full-screen game container, canvas, start overlay, HUD, and bottom control panel.
- **Config block:** editable colors for theme, skin tone, and hair color.
- **Audio manager:** unlocks Web Audio/HTML audio after interaction; maps start/toggle/randomize/click sounds to remote URLs.
- **Input and state logic:** `START` and `PLAY` state, button listeners, toggle handlers, Quick Mix randomization.
- **Rendering:** procedural background, character drawing, particles, and continuous `requestAnimationFrame` loop.
- **Feedback:** text badge, GIF image slot, particles, and SFX.

## Gameplay heuristic

The game is best understood as a **one-screen dress-up interaction loop**:

1. Player taps to enter play.
2. Player toggles clothing pieces on/off.
3. Character immediately changes visually.
4. Feedback confirms the action.
5. Player experiments with combinations or taps Quick Mix.

The loop is expressive rather than goal-driven. Its challenge is not timing or reflex; it is playful visual experimentation.

## Remix-direction summary

The user prompt is `flappy bird`. Under the stage safety harness, this should be interpreted as **theme, world, character, and visual identity direction**, not permission to replace the game with a Flappy Bird physics clone.

The target remix should become:

**Flappy Fashion Aviary** — a bright bird-mascot styling studio where the player prepares a cheerful winged character for a five-stop sky parade. The existing outfit toggles become flight-fashion pieces such as a wing cape, tail shorts, cloud shoes, and feather bow. The background evolves through cloud closets, pipe-gate scenery, feather carnivals, neon night skies, and a golden finale.

## Preserve vs. change guidance

### Preserve

- The one-screen canvas architecture.
- The `START` → `PLAY` transition.
- Pointer/touch button controls.
- Outfit toggle semantics.
- Quick Mix semantics.
- Lack of fail state, score, collision, and physics hazards.
- Mobile-safe bottom panel layout.
- Continuous cosmetic render loop.
- Feedback HUD and particle feedback pattern.

### Change safely

- Title, subtitle, CTA, HUD copy, and button labels.
- Character appearance from fashion doll to bird mascot / bird-costumed performer.
- Outfit item names and silhouettes.
- Procedural background motifs.
- Particle motifs from sparkles to feathers/wind puffs.
- Color palettes by conceptual level.
- Feedback language and optional remote catalog media mapping.
- World framing and narrative.

### Do not change

- Do not add gravity, flapping physics, pipe collision, scoring, death, or pass-through gates.
- Do not turn the toggle buttons into twitch controls.
- Do not rewrite the main loop or collision model.
- Do not introduce new win/loss semantics.
- Do not use media files from `assets/`; use only catalog-approved remote media if media is needed.

## Five-level progression blueprint

The source has no explicit levels, so downstream stages should use **conceptual visual progression** first. If later stages create level variants, they must remain direct-play styling variants and preserve the same mechanics.

1. **Cloud Closet Takeoff** — soft sky closet; teaches toggles and Quick Mix.
2. **Pipe Gate Preview** — decorative pipe arches appear as scenery only.
3. **Feather Carnival Crosswind** — fuller parade identity with feathers, banners, and richer feedback.
4. **Neon Night Flight** — high-energy night palette, glowing pipe props, star particles.
5. **Golden Sky Finale** — celebratory finale with spotlights, gold feathers, and award-ribbon HUD.

## Downstream priority

1. Ground the world as a bird-fashion sky parade.
2. Make the character recognizably birdlike using procedural art.
3. Replace boutique/styling copy with flight-fashion copy.
4. Add Flappy-recognizable sky, pipe, cloud, and feather motifs as non-hazard scenery.
5. Maintain mobile readability and protected mechanics.

# Blueprint

## Current game reality

The working clone currently contains a single-file HTML/CSS/JavaScript canvas game, `index.html`, titled **100 Clicks Cat**. It is a simple one-screen arcade clicker / target-tapping game.

### High-level code structure

- HTML shell with one full-screen `#game-container`.
- One `<canvas id="gameCanvas">` for all procedural gameplay visuals.
- UI overlay containing:
  - `#start-screen`
  - `#victory-screen`
  - `#hud`
  - noninteractive reaction badge/GIF layer
- Inline CSS for layout, glass panels, mobile HUD, buttons, and reaction overlays.
- Inline JavaScript modules by comment:
  1. assets/config
  2. audio system
  3. game state
  4. visuals
  5. game logic
  6. inputs

### Game loop / state model

The state flow is:

```text
start screen -> active gameplay -> victory screen -> restart -> active gameplay
```

During active gameplay, `requestAnimationFrame(gameLoop)` clears the canvas, draws the background, draws the cat target, updates the timer, draws particles, and continues while the game is active or particles remain. The player taps/clicks the target. A successful hit increments `score`, plays feedback, moves the target, and ends the game when `score >= 100`.

### Player goals

The player goal is to tap the target 100 times as fast as possible. There is no failure state and no countdown; elapsed time is performance feedback.

### Interaction pattern

- Start button unlocks audio and calls `initGame()`.
- Canvas `mousedown` and `touchstart` call `handleInput()`.
- `checkClick(x, y)` performs circular distance hit testing.
- Successful hit gives one point and relocates the cat.
- Victory at 100 successful hits.
- Restart button resets the loop.

### Core systems

- Canvas 2D procedural background.
- Canvas 2D procedural cat drawing.
- Distance-based hit detection.
- Random target relocation within safe viewport padding.
- Score HUD and timer HUD.
- Particle feedback.
- Reaction badge/GIF overlays.
- AudioController for BGM, victory loop, and SFX with user-gesture unlock.

### Inferred genre/gameplay shape

This is not currently Flappy Bird mechanically. It is best classified as a mobile-first target clicker/reflex tap game with spatial reacquisition and completion-time optimization.

## Intended remixed trajectory

The user remix prompt is **"flappy bird"**. Because the protected mechanics are target tapping, not flight physics, the safe remix trajectory is **Flappy Bird-inspired presentation over the existing 100-hit target loop**.

The intended remixed game should become **100 Flaps Bird**: a bright arcade sky training game where the player taps a round bird target 100 times to complete a flight rally. The target can visually become a flappy bird mascot; the world can include harmless pipes, clouds, feathers, medals, wind rings, rooftops, storms, and a golden nest finale.

## Preserve-vs-change guidance

### Preserve

- single full-screen canvas architecture
- start button -> active game -> victory screen -> restart flow
- mousedown/touchstart as primary input
- distance-based hit detection against one visible target
- one successful hit increments score by exactly one
- target relocates only after a successful hit
- TARGET_SCORE of 100 for canonical completion
- elapsed timer as performance feedback, not a fail countdown
- no miss penalty and no lose state
- mobile-safe HUD and CTA placement
- audio unlock on user gesture and nonblocking play/catch behavior

### Change safely

- title, subtitle, button labels, victory copy, badge text
- procedural target drawing: cat can become a recognizable flappy bird mascot while retaining same radius/hitbox
- background gradient/cloud/star layers can become side-scrolling sky, pipes-as-scenery, nests, city rooftops, storm clouds, or trophy aviary
- particles can become feathers, seed sparks, wind rings, or pixel stars
- HUD labels can become Wings, Flight Time, 100 Flaps, or Ring Count while preserving score/timer values
- remote audio/GIF mapping can use approved catalog URLs if later stages replace media
- color palette, typography, panel framing, and UI ornamentation
- progress milestone feedback at 1 and every 25 taps

## Five-level trajectory summary

1. **Cloud Hop Nursery**: simple morning training sky; bird target replaces cat.
2. **Pipe Garden Glide**: classic pipe scenery appears as noninteractive background.
3. **Rooftop Tailwind**: sunset town, wind rings, medal milestones.
4. **Storm Cloud Sprint**: storm atmosphere adds perceived pressure but no new penalties.
5. **Golden Nest Rally**: celebratory finale with trophy nest and gold feathers.

## Downstream warning

Do not reinterpret the prompt as permission to rebuild the game into a side-scrolling gravity/pipe collision clone. The current mechanics are coherent and mobile-safe; downstream stages should make the Flappy Bird identity through procedural art, copy, HUD, audio/visual feedback, and carefully staged presentation.

# Recreation Prompt

Create a mobile-first tap-based isometric game called **Flappy Sprout Sky Garden**. The game should feel visually inspired by Flappy Bird—bright blue skies, puffy clouds, green pipe-like trellises, and a tiny winged sprout-bird mascot—but it must keep the underlying gameplay as a cozy farming/resource loop rather than a flight-physics obstacle game.

The player starts from a polished title card, then enters a one-screen floating sky garden. A large readable HUD shows market funds, a seed-market button, and four touch-friendly tools: Plow, Plant, Water, and Harvest. The player taps a tool, then taps isometric floating garden tiles. Plow turns grass/cloud turf into soil, Plant places the currently equipped seed if the player can afford it, Water starts crop growth, and Harvest collects ripe crops for money. Watered crops grow over time; harvested crops return the tile to a reusable plowed state. Money is spent in a seed-market modal to unlock and equip better crops with higher seed costs, slower growth, and larger payouts.

Use procedural/code-native art wherever possible: canvas-drawn floating tiles, sprouts, wheat, corn, pumpkin-like sky produce, animated clouds, wind ribbons, pipe trellises, and a bouncy winged sprout mascot. Keep the controls large and mobile-safe, maintain the existing scoring and shop semantics, and avoid adding death, pipe collisions, jump physics, or side-scrolling. The progression should be framed as a five-world sky route: Calm Cloud Nursery, Pipe-Trellis Orchard, Gusty Market Route, Sunset Produce Aviary, and Storm-Crown Sky Bazaar. Each world should preserve the same mechanics while evolving background color, cloud density, pipe motifs, crop presentation, and HUD copy so the player recognizes progress without learning new controls.

# Blueprint

## Current game reality

### High-level code structure
- `index.html` is a self-contained HTML/CSS/JavaScript game.
- CSS defines a mobile-first glass HUD, start card, seed-market modal, tool buttons, and canvas backdrop.
- JavaScript defines:
  - `CROPS` data for wheat, corn, and pumpkin.
  - `AudioManager` with remote audio elements plus synthesized fallbacks.
  - Global state for money, grid cells, particles, floating text, selected tool, unlocked crops, active crop, camera, and timing.
  - A canvas render loop using `requestAnimationFrame`.
  - Isometric grid projection helpers.
  - Tile/crop drawing functions.
  - Pointer input routed to tile interactions.
  - Shop/crop unlock/equip UI logic.

### Game loop / state model
The player starts from a start overlay, opens the market, then uses four tools on an isometric grid:
1. Plow grass into soil.
2. Plant the active seed if the cell is plowed and the player has enough funds.
3. Water seeded crops so they begin growing.
4. Harvest ripe crops for money.

Growth advances over time only for watered seeded cells. Harvesting returns a cell to plowed state, allowing repeated planting cycles. Money unlocks higher-value crops in the seed market.

### Player goals
- Build funds by repeatedly planting, watering, waiting, and harvesting crops.
- Unlock better crops for larger payouts.
- Maintain a productive garden grid.

### Interaction pattern
- Tap/click tool buttons to choose a mode.
- Tap/click isometric tiles to apply the current tool.
- Open/close the market modal to unlock/equip crops.
- No keyboard-dependent controls are required.

### Core systems
- Isometric tile grid.
- Tool-based state transitions.
- Timed crop growth.
- Money economy.
- Crop unlock/equip shop.
- Canvas particle/floating-text feedback.
- Audio and GIF feedback for success/failure.
- Mobile responsive HUD and modal.

### Inferred genre/gameplay shape
The implemented game is a simple one-screen farming/resource clicker with light tycoon progression. It is not currently a Flappy Bird obstacle-avoidance game.

### Current identity summary
Current presentation is a bright blocky garden and seed-market fantasy with cheerful crops, glassy HUD panels, bouncy start-card art, and an isometric field.

## Intended remixed trajectory from prompt: “flappy bird”
Because the stage safety harness protects mechanics, the prompt should be interpreted as a presentation/narrative/theme direction rather than a license to convert the game into a physics flapper. The safest target is:

**A Flappy-bird-inspired sky-garden market where a tiny winged sprout/bird courier tends floating isometric garden plots between cheerful pipe-like trellises, cloud platforms, wind ribbons, and altitude-themed crop stalls.**

The interaction remains the same: tool selection, tile tapping, crop growth, harvesting, and crop unlocking. The remix changes character framing, backgrounds, props, HUD language, and level/world planning.

## Preserve-vs-change guidance

### Preserve
- Canvas render architecture.
- `requestAnimationFrame` main loop.
- Pointer/tap input model.
- Isometric grid math.
- Tool semantics: plow, seed, water, harvest.
- Crop growth timing model.
- Money scoring/economy.
- Shop unlock/equip semantics.
- Start screen, HUD, modal interaction paths.
- Audio unlock/fallback behavior.
- Mobile-first layout and large touch targets.

### Change safely downstream
- Title/copy/HUD wording.
- Crop icons/names/descriptions if values are preserved.
- Procedural background motifs: clouds, pipe-trellises, sky islands, wind trails.
- Procedural mascot art: winged sprout/bird gardener.
- Tile visual styling as floating sky plots.
- Particles and floating-text style.
- Shop theming as a sky nest/seed terminal.
- Five-level presentation and conceptual difficulty framing.

### Avoid
- Replacing the farming loop with jump/flap physics.
- Adding collision pipes or death states.
- Rewriting input to continuous tapping for flight.
- Changing crop prices, growth rules, unlock semantics, or scoring unless a later stage intentionally implements safe variants.
- Broad JavaScript refactors.

# Blueprint

## Current game reality

The implemented game in `index.html` is **Candy Drop**, a one-screen mobile-first physics puzzle. It is closer to *Cut the Rope* than to an implemented Flappy Bird clone. A candy object is suspended from procedurally generated rope segments. The player starts the game by tapping/clicking, then swipes across rope segments to cut them. Verlet physics, gravity, friction, and rope constraints move the candy. The candy can collect three stars for 100 points each, win by reaching the green monster mouth target, or lose by leaving the screen bounds.

## High-level code structure

- Single self-contained `index.html`.
- CSS defines full-screen mobile layout, glass UI, start screen, HUD, game-over panel, and lightweight effects.
- Remote catalog-approved audio/GIF URLs are embedded directly.
- `AudioManager` handles unlock, BGM, decoded SFX, and oscillator fallbacks.
- `VPoint` and `VStick` implement Verlet-style point/stick rope physics.
- `Game` owns state, canvas resize, input, level generation, update, draw, scoring, win/loss, particles, and the animation loop.

## Game loop / state model

State names: `START`, `PLAYING`, `WIN`, `GAMEOVER`.

1. `DOMContentLoaded` creates `window.game`.
2. Constructor sizes canvas, registers pointer/restart handlers, creates a demo layout, and starts `requestAnimationFrame`.
3. Pointerdown in `START` starts play.
4. During `PLAYING`, pointermove draws a cutting trail and tests intersections against active rope sticks.
5. Each frame updates physics, solves constraints, checks stars, checks goal win, checks out-of-bounds fail, updates particles, then redraws.
6. Win/loss pauses BGM, plays feedback, shows a GIF, updates result copy, and reveals the game-over panel.

## Player goals and interaction pattern

The player should guide the falling/swinging candy into the goal by cutting the correct rope segment at the correct time. Optional mastery comes from collecting stars before landing. The control pattern is one-finger mobile swipe, not button control.

## Core systems

- Protected input system: pointerdown/move/up.
- Protected physics system: Verlet point/stick constraints.
- Protected collision system: line intersection for cutting and circle distance checks for collectibles/goal.
- Protected scoring system: +100 per collected star.
- Protected round outcome system: win at goal, fail out of bounds.
- Themable presentation system: UI copy, colors, canvas art, background motifs, particles, and character silhouettes.

## Inferred genre/gameplay shape

Simple one-screen arcade physics puzzle with timing and spatial prediction. It is not a scrolling endless runner and does not have actual flap input, pipes as collision hazards, or continuous forward motion.

## Current identity summary

The current identity is a candy-themed sky puzzle: winged candy, ropes, stars, friendly green monster mouth, pastel gradients, sweet UI, and approved audio/GIF feedback.

## Remix-direction summary

The user prompt is `flappy bird`. The safe remix trajectory is **Flappy Candy Rescue**: a Flappy-inspired sky rescue puzzle where the winged candy becomes a tiny candy-bird, ropes become wind ribbons, stars become feathers, and the monster target becomes a hungry nest creature. Backgrounds can include clouds, green pipe-gate silhouettes, flock motifs, and sky migration progression. This should borrow Flappy Bird's visual vocabulary while preserving the implemented cut-rope mechanics.

## Preserve-vs-change guidance

### Preserve

- Swipe-to-cut controls.
- Verlet physics and rope constraints.
- Rope intersection cutting.
- Star/goal distance checks.
- Score semantics.
- Win/loss semantics.
- Canvas animation loop.
- Mobile pointer reliability.

### Change safely

- Title, CTA, HUD, win/loss text.
- Candy/monster/star/rope/peg visual framing.
- Procedural sky background.
- Particle colors and motifs.
- Five-level planning language and future visual progression.

### Do not change in this stage

- Do not convert the game into tap-to-flap.
- Do not add pipe collision hazards.
- Do not rewrite the main loop or physics.
- Do not create derived level files in this inference stage unless a later adapter stage explicitly requires it.

# Blueprint

## Current game reality

The workspace currently contains a single-browser `index.html` game titled **Neon Pet Parade**. It is implemented as a full-viewport HTML/CSS/Canvas game with inline JavaScript. The actual game is not a Flappy Bird clone mechanically; it is a simple one-screen mascot clicker.

### High-level code structure

- HTML document with:
  - catalog-approved remote font links
  - inline CSS for sky/glass UI/start overlay/HUD/GIF feedback
  - `application/x-game-config` block for `basePoints`, `unlockMultiplier`, and `bgColor`
  - hidden audio declarations using approved remote URLs
  - one canvas
  - start overlay
  - score / next-goal HUD
  - temporary unlock message
  - GIF feedback elements
- Inline JavaScript that:
  - parses config
  - initializes audio after user gesture
  - tracks game state, score, unlock threshold, skin index, particles, and mascot spring feedback
  - resizes canvas to viewport and DPR
  - handles pointer input
  - updates spring/particle physics
  - renders background, mascot, and particles in a requestAnimationFrame loop

## Game loop / state model

The state model is minimal:

1. `START`: the animated background renders behind a start overlay.
2. `PLAY`: the overlay hides, HUD appears, taps inside the mascot hit radius increase score and may trigger unlocks.
3. Temporary notification state: `unlock-msg` appears for two seconds after a threshold.

There is no implemented pause state, game-over state, fail state, win screen, obstacle state, or multi-level router.

## Player goals

- Start the parade.
- Tap the central mascot accurately.

Create a mobile-friendly canvas arcade runner called **Flappy Sky Sprint: Feather Gate Dash**.

The game should feel visually inspired by Flappy Bird while preserving a richer side-scrolling platformer/runner structure. ### Current identity summary
The source identity is a straightforward Flappy Bird clone: a cute bird, sky/ground backdrop, green pipe-like obstacles, tap-to-flap instructions, score survival, and game-over/retry loop.

## Intended remixed trajectory

The user prompt is `flappy bird`. Because the source is already Flappy Bird-like, the safest remix direction is not to replace the mechanics but to strengthen the game into a more authored, polished, level-aware Flappy Bird fantasy. The remix should keep the exact flap/pipe/score loop while expanding the presentation into a five-stage sky migration journey.

### Target remixed identity
**Title direction:** Flappy Bird: Skyway Migration  
A procedural, animated, code-native Flappy Bird world where the same bird travels through five increasingly intense skyway regions. Pipes are reframed as themed gateway hazards. The world evolves visually from sunrise meadows to storm-lit neon sky ruins, while the protected mechanics remain identical.

- Tap/click/Space flap input semantics.
- Gravity, flap impulse, bird motion feel, and collision model.
- Pipe spawning, scrolling, pass-through scoring, and game-over semantics.
- Start/pause/game-over/retry state flow.
- Canvas-based rendering architecture.
- Mobile actionability and one-action readability.

Change safely later:
- Bird character styling and procedural shape details.
- Pipe visual motif while keeping hitboxes unchanged.
- Background layers, sky colors, clouds, parallax, particles, and world props.
- UI copy, labels, HUD styling, and level/world labels.
- Audio mapping if using approved catalog media or existing safe hooks.
- Conceptual five-level presentation/difficulty framing through safe exposed constants only if downstream code confirms them.

Do not change:
- Collision geometry without explicit repair need.
- Scoring conditions.
- Fail/win/loss semantics.
- The core animation loop or state machine structure.
- Input semantics or controls.
- Mobile tap target reliability.

## Downstream implementation priority
1. Preserve the current Flappy Bird loop exactly.
2. Replace generic/default presentation with an authored procedural sky-migration identity.
3. Add clear five-level/world planning through safe visual and copy hooks before any mechanics tuning.
4. Use visual evolution to imply progression even if the executable remains endless.
5. Verify mobile controls, start/restart/pause, and game-over flows before adding polish.

# Blueprint

## Current Game Reality

The current codebase is a single-file HTML5 canvas game in `index.html`. It implements a responsive one-screen word-search puzzle called **Signal Sweep**.

### High-level Code Structure
- Inline CSS defines full-screen layout, HUD panels, feedback overlays, mobile adjustments, and visual styling.
- A JSON config script provides `gridSize`, `themeColor`, and `accentColor`.
- Audio elements provide background music and scan/success/fail/win cues.
- Inline JavaScript handles:
  - config parsing
  - audio unlock and playback
  - word-grid generation
  - target word state
  - pointer drag input
  - straight-line word matching
  - particles, shake, and background animation
  - canvas render loop
  - responsive sizing via `ResizeObserver`

### Game Loop / State Model
The state model is intentionally compact:
- `STARTING` while booting
- `PLAYING` while the player searches and drags through the grid
- `GAMEOVER` when all target words are found and the completion panel appears

The loop is:
1. Generate a 7x7 grid and target words.
2. Render animated background, grid, letters, found highlights, current drag, and particles.
3. Player drags through cells.
4. Submitted line is checked against target words forward and backward.
5. Correct words are marked found; incorrect words trigger recoverable feedback.
6. When all target words are found, show the completion panel.
7. Pressing the button increments level and starts another sector.

### Player Goals
Find every target word listed in the HUD.

### Interaction Pattern
Mobile-safe pointer dragging across grid cells. The player can use mouse or touch. Valid selections are straight horizontal, vertical, or diagonal lines.

### Core Systems
- Random word placement
- Target word HUD
- Drag-line calculation
- Word matching
- Found-word highlighting
- Completion overlay
- Audio/haptic/visual feedback
- Responsive canvas metrics

### Inferred Genre / Gameplay Shape
Primary genre: word search puzzle. Secondary shape: casual one-screen mobile puzzle with arcade-style sensory feedback.

### Current Identity Summary
The current presentation is a neon radar / signal-ops interface. The word list is mostly nature/calm words, but the HUD calls them call signs and sectors.

## Intended Remixed Trajectory

User remix prompt: **harry potter**

The safest intended remix is **Spell Sweep: Wizarding Word Quest**: a wizarding-school spell-tracing word search where the grid becomes enchanted parchment, target words become spells/clues/artifacts, dragging becomes wand tracing, and level progression becomes a five-lesson journey through recognizable magical-school spaces.

## Preserve-vs-Change Guidance

### Preserve
- Canvas render loop structure and ResizeObserver-driven sizing
- 7x7 grid default unless downstream variants intentionally use the existing config knob
- Pointer drag input semantics
- Straight horizontal/vertical/diagonal selection validation
- Forward/reversed word matching
- Found-word state and all-targets-found completion
- Incorrect-selection recoverability with no loss state
- Level increments via restart/continue button
- Audio unlock on first user interaction
- Mobile-safe HUD and canvas layout

### Change / Theme Safely
- Title, HUD labels, level naming, instruction copy, result copy, button copy
- WORD_BANK replacement with themed spell/class/artifact words if done later without changing matching logic
- Canvas colors, gradients, tile styling, selection pill colors, particles
- Background floating motifs and ambient animation
- Feedback captions and approved GIF/audio mapping
- CSS typography using approved catalog fonts
- Procedural props such as candles, stars, owls, castle windows, wand sparks, house banners

## Remix Direction Summary
Downstream stages should not create a combat game, runner, RPG, or physics spell simulator. They should preserve the word-search mechanics and strengthen the Harry Potter-inspired identity through procedural magical art, copy, HUD styling, target-word vocabulary, and five visually distinct lesson/world beats.

# Blueprint

## Current Game Reality

`index.html` implements **Arcade Brain Sprint**, a single-file mobile-first timed quiz arcade game. The codebase is organized as inline CSS, DOM screens, audio elements, a canvas background renderer, and JavaScript modules/objects:

- `CONFIG`: languages, quiz lane labels, localization strings.
- `state`: selected language/theme/difficulty/question count, score, question index, correct/missed counts, timer, generated questions, playing flag.
- `AudioSys`: unlocks audio on user gesture, controls looping BGM and SFX for UI, start, correct, wrong, warning, and results.
- `Visuals`: owns the canvas background loop plus confetti and shake feedback.
- `Game`: binds DOM events, renders language/setup/ranking screens, generates arithmetic questions, starts/advances/ends runs, updates score and leaderboard.

The active game loop is protected: choose language, open menu, configure quiz lane/difficulty/round count, start a timed run, answer four-button arithmetic questions before a per-question timer expires, receive feedback, advance to the next question, then see final score and local leaderboard.

## State Model

Likely screens:
1. Language select
2. Main menu
3. Setup
4. Gameplay
5. Results
6. Ranking/leaderboard

State transitions are DOM class toggles through `showScreen(id)`. Gameplay progression is `qIdx / questions.length`.

## Player Goals

The player tries to maximize score by answering generated arithmetic prompts correctly. Difficulty affects points awarded per correct answer, not the arithmetic range or timer. Question count affects run length.

## Interaction Pattern

All meaningful input is button/touch based. The gameplay verb is selecting one of four answer buttons. The setup slider adjusts round count. This must remain mobile-first and large-target.

## Core Systems

- Arithmetic question generator with `+`, `-`, and `*`.
- Four answer options: one correct, three random nearby distractors.
- Per-question timer.
- Correct/wrong/timeout feedback.
- Score/correct/missed tracking.
- localStorage leaderboard.
- Canvas background and feedback particles.
- Audio hooks for core feedback states.

## Inferred Genre / Gameplay Shape

Simple timed quiz arcade / quiz game with a mobile-first one-screen playfield and menu shell.

## Current Identity Summary

The current presentation is neon arcade coaching: cyber grid, mascot face, cyan/violet panels, “Arcade Brain Sprint,” “Quiz Comet,” and rapid-fire number drills.

## Intended Remixed Trajectory

The remix prompt is `harry potter`. The safe intended target is a **Harry Potter-inspired wizarding school spell exam quiz sprint**. The player becomes a student earning house points by answering enchanted arithmetic spell prompts before the hourglass runs out. The game should feel like a magical castle journey through classrooms, potions, forest, Quidditch-style cup energy, and a Great Hall final exam.

## Preserve vs Change Guidance

### Preserve
- Question generation and four-answer selection.
- Timer, timeout, wrong/correct feedback semantics.
- Difficulty scoring semantics.
- Round count and progression.
- Menu/setup/game/result/ranking flow.
- Canvas + DOM architecture.
- Mobile safe-area and tap-target layout.

### Change Safely Later
- Title/copy/HUD labels.
- Quiz lane labels.
- Colors, panel styling, procedural canvas world, particles.
- Feedback metaphors and SFX/media URLs using approved catalogs only.
- Conceptual level/world framing.

### Do Not Overinterpret
Do not turn this into combat, flying, parkour, potion mixing, or a movement game. The remix should be recognizable through art direction, narrative framing, UI copy, and procedural animated wizard-school environments while the timed quiz mechanics remain intact.

# Blueprint

## Current game reality

`index.html` implements **Blocky Garden: Seed Market**, a self-contained isometric farming and seed-market simulator.

High-level code structure:
- HTML/CSS shell with responsive full-screen canvas, start screen, HUD, tool strip, shop modal, GIF feedback overlay, and audio tags.
- `CROPS` data defines wheat, corn, and pumpkin with icon, color, seed cost, unlock price, sell price, growth time, and description.
- `AudioManager` loads remote audio, unlocks on user gesture, plays BGM/SFX, and synthesizes fallback tones.
- Game state tracks `money`, `grid`, `particles`, `floatingTexts`, `currentTool`, `unlockedCrops`, `activeCropId`, `lastTime`, and `camera`.
- Grid/camera math uses `isoToScreen` and `screenToIso` to map pointer taps onto isometric tiles.
- The loop updates crop growth and feedback particles, then draws sky, tiles, crops, particles, and floating texts.
- UI functions update money, select tools, open/close the shop, unlock crops, and equip crops.

## Current gameplay loop

The player opens the market, then:
1. Selects **Plow** and taps grass tiles to turn them into plowed beds.
2. Selects **Plant** and taps plowed beds to spend the active seed cost and place a crop.
3. Selects **Water** and taps seeded crops to begin growth.
4. Waits as watered crops mature according to crop growth timers.
5. Selects **Pick/Harvest** and taps ripe crops to earn money.
6. Opens the seed market to unlock or equip higher-value crops.
7. Repeats for more profit.

There is no terminal fail state. Invalid actions trigger error SFX, fail GIF feedback, and sometimes floating text like “Need Funds!”

## Inferred genre/gameplay shape

Simple-to-medium farming simulator / resource-management loop with timed growth and shop-based crop progression.

## Current identity summary

The game is bright, blocky, garden-themed, and market-oriented: cheerful crops, sunny sky, green/soil palette, cash score, seed market, and produce stall copy.

## Intended remixed trajectory

Remix prompt: `harry potter`.

The target should become **Hogwarts Herbology Market**: a magical Herbology greenhouse where the existing farm actions are reframed as preparing enchanted beds, planting magical seeds, casting Aguamenti to water, harvesting potion ingredients, and spending Galleons or Herbology Funds in a Hogwarts seed cabinet / Hogsmeade apothecary stall.

## Preserve-vs-change guidance

Preserve:
- Isometric grid, tile states, and coordinate math.
- Tool actions and validity rules.
- Crop growth timers and watering requirement.
- Money, seed cost, sell price, unlock, and equip semantics.
- Start screen, HUD, shop modal, particle/floating text feedback, audio trigger timing, and mobile layout.

Change safely:
- Copy, title, labels, crop names/descriptions/icons/colors.
- UI panel styling, parchment/house crest look, background gradients.
- Procedural crop drawings and ambient canvas/CSS motifs.
- Market framing from produce stand to Herbology/apothecary cabinet.
- Conceptual five-level visual/progression framing.

Do not add combat, enemies, collision hazards, health, countdown failure, avatar movement, spell inventory, or new RPG systems.

The player is a young witch or wizard moving through five magical school trials: a first wand lesson, a moving staircase hallway, a potion lab, a stormy broom-practice pitch, and a moonlit forbidden forest finale. # Blueprint — Remix Inference Plus

## Current game reality

The working game is a full-screen, portrait-first, one-screen canvas/DOM arcade story. The canvas continuously renders an animated neon boardroom scene with two central characters, a lower decorative hero token, particles, drifting petals, and parallax background shapes. The active gameplay is not collision-based: the player reads a prompt and taps one of two bottom buttons.

### High-level code structure
- `index.html` contains all CSS, DOM, configuration, audio elements, canvas drawing, input handling, state management, and game loop.
- `#game-config` exposes `heroSpeed` and `themeColor`.
- JavaScript initializes on `DOMContentLoaded`, sizes via `ResizeObserver`, then runs a `requestAnimationFrame` loop.
- State is represented by `gameState` with `PLAYING` and `GAMEOVER`.
- Progress is represented by `storyIndex`, `score`, and `lives`.
- Story content is held in the `storyNodes` array.
- HUD and choice buttons are DOM elements over the canvas.

### Game loop / state model
1. Boot canvas and initialize score/lives/story.
2. Render animated background, characters, hero token, particles, and flashes.
3. Wait for player to tap choice A or B.
4. Correct choice: +20 score, success sound/GIF/particles, light vibration.
5. Wrong choice: -1 life, fail sound/GIF/particles, shake/flash/vibration.
6. Advance to the next story node.
7. If lives reach 0, show game-over overlay and restart button.

### Player goals
The player tries to keep Composure and earn Clout by choosing the best response in each social prompt.

### Interaction pattern
The real interaction is two-choice tapping. Canvas pointer movement moves the lower hero marker horizontally, but this is decorative and not required to solve the prompts.

### Core systems
- Two-option choice system.
- Fixed five-node story progression.
- Score/lives HUD.
- Game-over/restart.
- Canvas procedural rendering.
- Audio unlock and SFX/BGM.
- Feedback particles, GIF overlays, flashes, shake, vibration bridge.

### Inferred genre/gameplay shape
Simple one-screen mobile arcade / interactive visual-novel-choice hybrid. It resembles a compact dialogue quiz with arcade feedback.

### Current identity summary
The current theme is “Boardroom Hearts: Meme Arcade”: a neon business/romance meme boardroom where correct social replies create clout.

## Intended remixed trajectory

### Remix direction summary
The prompt “harry potter” should transform the presentation into a recognizable wizard-school magical-choice adventure while preserving the underlying two-choice story mechanics. The safest target is an original Hogwarts-inspired school-year journey: earn House Points, keep Focus, choose wise spells and loyal responses, and progress through five magical trials.

### Preserve-vs-change guidance
Preserve:
- Two-choice DOM controls.
- Score/life semantics.
- Story node advancement.
- PLAYING/GAMEOVER states.
- Restart behavior.
- Mobile layout.
- Canvas render loop and update/render architecture.

Change safely:
- Title, HUD labels, prompt/option copy.
- Canvas art: castle, classrooms, candles, wands, potions, staircases, quidditch-like pitch, forest.
- CSS palette and panel styling.
- Feedback visual language: sparks, spell fizzles, house-point bursts.
- Optional remote media from catalog files only.

Avoid:
- Adding combat, spell aiming, dodging, collision, inventory, timers, or new rules.
- Rewriting the main loop.
- Using assets/ media.
- Relying on copyrighted screenshots or unapproved URLs.

## Downstream implementation heuristic
Treat the current `storyNodes` as the five-level spine. Each node can become a magical trial. Later stages should build an authored procedural world around that spine instead of making new mechanics. Visual complexity can increase across nodes/levels through backgrounds, motifs, particles, and UI copy, while the player still only needs to read and tap.

# RecreationPrompt.md

Create a mobile-first one-screen canvas physics sandbox called **Hogwarts Spell Swarm Collider**. The player is a Hogwarts student practicing advanced charms by touching and dragging anywhere on the playfield to cast glowing spell motes. Each mote behaves like a small physics particle: it drifts, attracts other motes, collides, bounces off the field edges, glows, and contributes to the displayed total. The experience has no traditional fail state; the goal is to grow, shape, and enjoy a readable magical swarm.

Keep the interaction model simple and always visible. A magical HUD shows **Charm Power** and **Motes**. Large buttons let the player cycle the next spell color through Hogwarts house-inspired hues, hold time, run at 1X/2X/3X, pulse the swarm with a wand flourish, clear/reset the field with a finite-style incantation, and open an audio/graphics settings panel. Preserve the original mechanics: pointer spawning, N-body attraction, collision response, pulse impulse, time scaling, reset, score/count semantics, and mobile-safe controls.

Present the game as a five-beat Hogwarts journey without requiring new mechanics: **First Charms Lesson**, **Moving Staircase Drift**, **Great Hall House Convergence**, **Forbidden Forest Patronus Trial**, and **Astronomy Tower Final Conjunction**. The worlds should feel progressively more magical and visually distinct while remaining one shared game family. Use procedural CSS/canvas/SVG art rather than stock images as the main identity: floating candles, parchment panels, house banners, spell circles, wand trails, Marauder's Map footprints, castle silhouettes, Patronus mist, tree silhouettes, telescope shapes, Time-Turner rings, and star constellations.

Prioritize readability and mobile actionability. Background animation should be beautiful but low contrast behind active spell motes. Do not add enemies, health, combat rules, platforming, inventory, quests, or win/loss conditions. The final result should feel like a tactile magical particle toy set in Hogwarts: immediately playable, luminous, recognizable, and safely faithful to the original physics loop.

# Blueprint.md — Remix Inference Plus

## Current game reality

The codebase is a single-file HTML/CSS/JavaScript canvas game named **Graviton Micro Collider**. It uses a fixed full-window `<canvas>` and an overlaid DOM HUD/settings layer. The core simulation is an N-body particle field:

- `Particle` objects have position, velocity, mass `1`, radius `4`, color, and glow phase.
- Pointer down/move/up on the canvas controls continuous particle spawning at the pointer.
- `physicsStep()` applies pairwise gravity, friction, movement, boundary bounce, and circle collision response.
- `loop()` runs through `requestAnimationFrame`, applies `timeScale`, draws the space-like background, input ring, and all particles.
- HUD values show `SWARM` as `totalMass` and `ORBS` as `particles.length`.
- Buttons cycle color, set time scale (`HOLD`, `1X`, `2X`, `3X`), pulse the swarm, reset the field, and open a control/settings modal.
- Audio is handled by HTML audio/Web Audio buffers plus small synthesized spawn sounds.
- There is no explicit health, fail state, target, enemy, round clear, or level system.

## Gameplay heuristic

The player creates, observes, and perturbs a chaotic swarm. The minimum loop is:

1. Touch/drag the canvas to spawn particles.
2. Watch gravity pull particles together.
3. Use pulse/time controls to agitate or inspect the swarm.
4. Reset or recolor when desired.
5. Treat the increasing count/mass as progress.

This is a one-screen physics sandbox with arcade-like feedback, not a win/loss action game.

## High-level code structure

- HTML shell: canvas, HUD, feedback layer, settings modal, audio tags, config JSON script.
- CSS: full-screen layout, glass HUD cards, interactive buttons, modal, feedback GIF treatment, mobile responsive sizing.
- JavaScript state: canvas context, dimensions, particles, time scale, sound/graphics options, pointer state, color palette, config proxy.
- Audio layer: Web Audio buffer loading, background music resume, SFX playback, synthesized spawn tone, vibration bridge.
- Simulation layer: `Particle`, `initGame`, `spawnParticle`, `physicsStep`, `moveChunk`, `draw`, `loop`.
- Input/lifecycle layer: resize observer, pointer events, button listeners, settings controls.

## Current identity summary

The current identity is sci-fi: micro collider, swarm/orbs, control deck, signal, neon nebula background, impact feedback, and electronic audio. The presentation suggests a space-lab particle toy.

## Intended remixed trajectory

The remix prompt is **Harry Potter**. The safe target is **Hogwarts Spell Swarm Collider**: a magical training sandbox where the particles become spell motes/charms, the pointer becomes wand casting, color cycling becomes house/spell signal selection, pulse becomes a wand flourish, time controls become Time-Turner/tempo charms, and reset becomes a clearing incantation.

The remix should be recognizable through Hogwarts-inspired procedural art: castle silhouettes, Great Hall candles, house-color banners, Marauder's Map lines, Patronus mist, astronomy motifs, spell rings, wand trails, and parchment/gold UI treatment.

## Preserve vs change guidance

### Preserve

- Canvas game loop and `requestAnimationFrame` structure.
- Pointer spawning semantics.
- N-body gravity, friction, movement, boundary bounce, and collision response.
- `timeScale` button meanings.
- Pulse and reset behavior.
- Score/count numeric semantics.
- Mobile-first overlay and settings actionability.
- Audio toggle and graphics toggle behavior.

### Change safely

- Title, labels, HUD copy, feedback copy.
- CSS colors, panel styling, fonts if approved/remote/catalog-safe.
- Canvas background and particle visual treatment, provided radius/collision behavior stays intact.
- Color palette mapping to Hogwarts house/spell colors.
- Conceptual five-level framing as presentation/progression guidance.
- Feedback labels and approved remote media slot choices.

### Do not overinterpret

Do not add enemies, health, spell combat, collectible quests, RPG inventory, cutscenes, platforming, trivia, or fail states in this stage. Complexity should come from staged visual world identity and clearer magical feedback, not new mechanics.

## Downstream implementation summary

Later stages should transform the game into a recognizable procedural Hogwarts spell-swarm experience while keeping the existing physics sandbox untouched. The five-world plan should be used as authored visual/progression guidance: Charms classroom, Moving Staircases, Great Hall, Forbidden Forest Patronus trial, and Astronomy Tower conjunction.

# Blueprint — Remix Inference Plus

## High-level code structure

The current game is a single-file HTML5 Canvas game in `index.html`.

- CSS defines full-screen mobile-safe layout, start/game-over panels, HUD, mute button, and feedback GIF placement.
- `ASSETS` lists remote image, audio, and GIF URLs.
- `AudioManager` handles preload/unlock/play/stop/mute for BGM and SFX.
- Canvas code defines `Bubble`, `Projectile`, and `Particle` classes.
- Game state uses `START`, `PLAY`, and `GAMEOVER`.
- Core functions include `initGame`, `spawnProjectile`, `handleLanding`, `findMatches`, `dropFloatingBubbles`, `getNeighbors`, `createExplosion`, `gameOver`, `resize`, `draw`, `update`, and input/start/restart handlers.

## Game identity and current behavior

### Current game reality

- Title: **Sky Signal Relay**
- Genre / archetype: **bubble shooter / match-3 projectile puzzle**
- Core player goal: drag to aim and release to launch colored orbs into a hex grid, matching 3+ same-color orbs, dropping disconnected clusters, scoring points, and avoiding the lower loss threshold.
- Core verb: **drag to aim; release to launch**.
- Fail state: if a landed bubble reaches row `GRID_ROWS - 2`, `gameOver()` shows the game-over screen and stops BGM.
- Success / score state: matched bubbles score `matches.length * 10`; dropped floating bubbles score `dropped * 20`; an empty grid loops by calling `initGame()`.
- Camera / viewport assumptions: full-screen canvas sized to `window.innerWidth/innerHeight`, with mobile viewport and safe-area-aware UI.
- Input model: pointer/mouse/touch drag and release on the canvas, plus start/restart/mute buttons.
- Moment-to-moment loop: start → initialize 5 random rows → drag aim → release projectile → projectile bounces/snaps → BFS match check → pop/drop/score or danger/loss → spawn next projectile → render.
- Screen states: `START`, `PLAY`, `GAMEOVER`; mute control is always available.
- Current progression: no explicit level progression; clearing the board starts a new board.

# Blueprint.md

## Current game reality

The working game is `Creature Laboratory`, implemented as a single `index.html` containing CSS, DOM UI, a full-window `<canvas>`, and JavaScript. It is a simple creature creator / pet simulator toy rather than a challenge game.

### High-level code structure

- HTML shell:
  - `#game-container`
  - `#gameCanvas`
  - start overlay
  - lab controls
  - play/reset controls
  - interaction bar
  - HUD/status
  - GIF feedback overlay
- CSS:
  - responsive full-screen layout
  - glassy sci-fi/neon panels
  - bottom mobile control strips
  - compact HUD and reset controls
- JavaScript:
  - asset URL table
  - `AudioController`
  - global game state (`phase`, selected options, particles, creature)
  - option definitions (`SPECIES`, `COLORS`, `SIZES`)
  - rendering functions (`drawLab`, `drawRoom`, `drawCreature`, `drawParticles`)
  - animation loop (`gameLoop`)
  - DOM event handlers for start, create, reset, pet, feed, scare, and canvas tap

## Game loop / state model

The protected state model is:

1. Start overlay.
2. Lab phase:
   - Player chooses species, color, and size from a horizontal option strip.
   - Canvas shows cauldron/lab art and particles.
3. Create creature:
   - `phase` changes from `lab` to `room`.
   - Creature receives the selected traits.
   - Lab controls hide; reset and care buttons appear.
4. Observation room:
   - Creature idles, walks, blinks, eats, becomes happy, or becomes scared.
   - Player can pet, feed, scare, tap creature, or reset.
5. Reset:
   - Returns to lab phase with controls restored.

There is no score, timer, explicit level, win, loss, health, enemy, or resource economy.

## Player goals

The player goal is expressive and playful:
- create a creature with chosen traits;
- observe how it looks and moves;
- trigger reactions through pet/feed/scare;
- repeat the experiment.

## Interaction pattern

- Button-first mobile-safe UI.
- Tap/click selections.
- Tap creature on canvas as a shortcut for petting.
- No precision movement or drag controls.

## Core systems

- Procedural canvas rendering.
- Trait selection.
- Creature state machine.
- Particle feedback.
- Audio feedback.
- Lightweight remote GIF reaction overlay.
- Responsive DOM overlay HUD and controls.

## Inferred genre/gameplay shape

Best genre description: pet simulator / creature creator / avatar toy. It has traces of dress-up customization and companion interaction, but it is not a puzzle, runner, shooter, combat game, or resource simulator.

## Current identity summary

The current presentation is a neon sci-fi creature laboratory: DNA, serums, glowing cauldron, observation room, and lab safety copy.

## Remix-direction summary: Harry Potter

The Harry Potter remix direction should transform the same structure into a magical-school familiar forge. The lab becomes a Hogwarts-like potions classroom. Species become magical familiar lineages. Color becomes house-aura/charm color. Size becomes charm strength. The observation room becomes a castle common room, creature-care yard, forest edge, or astronomy tower depending on level/world framing.

## Preserve-vs-change guidance

### Preserve

- Start -> lab -> room flow.
- Selection dimensions: species, color, size.
- Create/reset/care actions.
- Pointer/touch semantics.
- Creature movement/state timers.
- Feed growth behavior.
- No failure/scoring unless a later stage explicitly and safely adds only presentation-level goals.
- Full-window canvas with DOM overlay controls.

### Change safely

- Title, copy, labels, icons.
- CSS palette and panel styling.
- Canvas background art and decorative props.
- Particle style and HUD wording.
- Procedural creature silhouettes as long as branch structure remains stable.
- Audio/GIF mappings only if using approved catalog remote media.

## Intended remixed trajectory

Target result: `Hogwarts Familiar Forge`, a cozy magical-school pet creator where the player brews a familiar in a potions classroom, chooses magical aura and charm scale, then bonds with the familiar through touch, treats, and playful startle magic. Five planned visual worlds/lessons carry the same mechanics from first-year potions to a final astronomy tower showcase.

# Blueprint

## Current game reality

`index.html` implements **Forge Run: Iron Trial**, a mobile-first top-down survival-crafting game in a single HTML file. The structure is:

- CSS utility classes, UI theme styling, joystick styling, HUD/modal/start/game-over overlays.
- A full-screen `<canvas>` renderer.
- Inline module script with configuration, audio loading, state, procedural map generation, joystick control, update loop, entity interactions, crafting, smelting minigame, UI updates, and canvas drawing.

The implemented loop is not a one-button runner or simple clicker. It is a medium arcade survival-crafting loop:

1. Start the run.
2. Move with a touch joystick.
3. Stop near resources so auto-harvesting can chip HP from entities.
4. Pick up drops to build inventory and recover small amounts of energy.
5. Open the craft modal to make tools, processed resources, and a furnace.
6. Use the cave entrance/ladder to switch between surface and cave.
7. Stand near the furnace to smelt copper/iron tools through a timed tap-target minigame.
8. Continue until energy reaches zero and game over reports copper/iron banked.

Current screen states are start, play HUD, crafting modal, crafting minigame, and game over. There is implicit progression through recipes and tool gates, but no explicit five-level selector.

## Intended remixed trajectory

The remix prompt is **Harry Potter**. The safest high-confidence direction is a Hogwarts magical fieldwork trial layered over the same survival-crafting mechanics. The player becomes a robed student gathering magical school materials around Hogwarts grounds, greenhouse yards, forest edges, vault caves, and a Room-of-Requirement forge. The furnace becomes a cauldron/forge. Ores and drops become wandwood, sparkstones, runic clay, charm metals, coal/iron spell cores, wool/meat energy supplies, and forged protective tools.

## Preserve vs change guidance

### Preserve

- Touch joystick and button/tap input.
- Game loop, update/draw architecture, and requestAnimationFrame flow.
- Tile collision and movement.
- Surface/cave map switching.
- Energy drain and game-over semantics.
- Inventory keys, recipe costs, craft logic, tool gates, furnace proximity.
- Auto-harvest cadence and target distance.
- Smelting minigame timing, target count, success/failure rules.
- Mobile-safe modal controls and audio unlock behavior.

### Change safely

- Title, recipe names, HUD labels, start copy, game-over text, floating text, feedback captions.
- Canvas colors and procedural silhouettes.
- UI palette/panels/buttons to parchment/gold/house-color magical styling.
- Entity visuals to robed student, wandwood trees, herb clumps, runic clay, cauldron forge, vault cave entrance, spell-core ores.

- Conceptual five-level progression language and later conservative level files if requested.

## Downstream priority

Later stages should implement theme by renaming and drawing, not by redesigning mechanics. The five-level plan should be a learning/world-journey frame over the existing crafting chain: Castle Grounds -> Greenhouse Yard -> Forbidden Forest Edge -> Vault Cave Passage -> Room of Requirement Iron Charm.

metadata.blueprint_markdown:
# Blueprint

## Current Game Reality

The source game is `Blue Rush vs Egg Boss`, a single-file canvas arcade boss fight in `index.html`. The player controls a Sonic-like runner with one pointer/tap action: jump from the ground or double-jump in the air. The hero automatically advances within a side-view arena while gravity, ground contact, spin-jump state, invulnerability frames, and recoil are handled by the existing loop. The boss floats at the right side of the screen, periodically spawns bouncing bombs, and has a 1000 HP boss bar. The player can damage the boss by stomping it from above for 50 damage or by stomping bombs to kick them back into the boss for 100 damage. Rings are the damage buffer: the player starts with 10 rings, collectible rings spawn from the right, contact with hazards/boss drains rings to 0 and grants invulnerability, and taking damage with 0 rings causes Game Over. Score increases from ring pickups (+10) and boss damage; victory occurs when boss HP reaches 0, with final score including remaining rings × 100. Screen states are START, PLAY, GAMEOVER, and VICTORY; UI includes start/restart buttons, rings, score, boss HP, audio, particles, and reaction GIF overlays.

## High-Level Code Structure

- `index.html`: the complete canonical game surface, including CSS, DOM overlays, audio tags, canvas, game state, update/draw loop, input handlers, and all entities.
- `catalogs/`: approved remote media catalog references for downstream media choices.
- `assets/`: local mirrors exist, but this workflow forbids using media from `assets/` for replacement; only CSS/JS from assets may be used if needed later.

## Game Loop / State Model

The game uses `requestAnimationFrame(loop)`, where `update()` runs only during `PLAY` and `draw()` renders continuously. State values are:

- `START`: start panel visible.
- `PLAY`: HUD visible; physics, boss, bombs, rings, particles, collisions, and score update.
- `GAMEOVER`: triggered by taking damage with 0 rings.
- `VICTORY`: triggered when boss HP reaches 0.

## Player Goals

Defeat the boss by timing jumps and double-jumps to:

1. stomp the boss from above for direct damage,
2. stomp falling/bouncing bombs to kick them back into the boss,
3. collect rings to maintain the damage buffer,
4. avoid unsafe side/body contact with bombs and the boss.

## Interaction Pattern

The source uses one core action: pointer/tap on the canvas to jump or double-jump. Start and restart are ordinary click buttons. No keyboard model is present in the inspected source.

## Core Systems

- One-button jump/double-jump control.
- Gravity, ground contact, spin state, recoil, and invulnerability frames.
- Boss with 1000 HP, floating movement, and periodic bomb spawning.
- Bomb state machine: `NORMAL` bombs hurt the hero unless stomped from above; stomped bombs become `KICKED` and damage the boss on contact.
- Rings as health buffer: rings drop to 0 on damage; damage at 0 rings causes game over.
- Ring collectibles and score.
- Canvas-only procedural rendering of sky, ground, rings, bombs, boss, hero, and particles.
- HUD and overlays for boss HP, rings, score, start, victory, game over, audio, and reaction GIFs.

## Inferred Genre / Gameplay Shape

Medium one-button side-view arcade boss fight with platformer/runner physics, timing-heavy stomp contacts, projectile reflection, ring-buffer survival, and a single arena.

## Current Identity Summary

Create a mobile-first one-screen wizard-school memory game called **Hogwarts Spell Recall**. The player is a young wizard practicing spell sequences at a magical castle. A round begins when the player taps a large start button. The game displays a short sequence of glowing colored spell runes in circular slots for a few seconds, then hides the unrecalled runes and shows six large stationary enchanted orbs. The player must tap the orbs in the exact same order to cast the charm.

# Blueprint — Remix Inference Plus

## Current game reality

### High-level code structure
- `index.html` is a self-contained HTML/CSS/JavaScript game.
- CSS defines the full-screen layout, glass HUD panels, modal styling, responsive mobile behavior, and visual theme variables.
- Hidden audio elements provide BGM and SFX sources, with a Web Audio / HTMLAudio fallback system and synthetic SFX fallback.
- A JSON `game-config` block exposes safe configuration values: `memorizeDuration`, `sequenceLength`, and `baseColor`.
- The canvas layer renders the actual game board: background, sequence slots, tap palette, glyph crystals, shake, and particles.
- DOM overlays handle the start/next/restart message box, HUD, feedback GIF layer, and shop modal.
- Local storage persists coins, owned visual themes, and the currently selected theme.

### Game loop / state model
The game uses a protected `requestAnimationFrame` loop with `update(dt)` and `draw()` phases. The state machine is:
- `IDLE`: message overlay is visible or the round is between active phases.
- `MEMORIZE`: the generated color sequence is visible for `memorizeDuration` seconds.
- `INPUT`: the sequence is hidden except already-correct entries, and the player taps palette orbs.
- `GAMEOVER`: lives are depleted and restart is offered.

### Player goals
The player studies the displayed sequence of colored crystals and repeats it by tapping six circular color orbs in the same order. The short-term goal is to complete the current sequence. The long-term meta-goal is to earn coins and unlock/select alternate visual themes.

### Interaction pattern
The interaction is single-pointer/touch memory recall. During `INPUT`, a canvas `pointerdown` is converted into canvas coordinates and matched against circular palette hit zones. DOM buttons are used for start, next, restart, shop open/close, buy, and use.

### Core systems
- Sequence generation from the active theme palette.
- Memorization timer and reveal/hide transition.
- Radial hit testing against palette orb centers.
- Correct/incorrect input resolution.
- Lives, coins, and persistent shop economy.
- Canvas rendering and particle feedback.
- Audio, vibration, and GIF feedback.
- Responsive full-window canvas sizing.

### Inferred genre/gameplay shape
This is a simple one-screen arcade memory game, closest to a Simon-style sequence recall loop, with light collectible/shop progression.

### Current identity summary
The current presentation is cyber/crystal themed: “Chroma Recall,” “Cipher Recall,” “Signal Locked,” “Trace Triggered,” neon glass UI, glowing glyph crystals, and loadout-lab visual themes.

## Intended remixed trajectory

### Remix direction summary
The user remix prompt is “Harry Potter.” The safest target is a wizard-school spell recall game where the same color-sequence memory mechanic becomes memorizing and recasting spell-rune sequences. The target title is **Hogwarts Spell Recall**. The player is a young wizard practicing charms, potions, Quidditch signals, forest light trails, and a final Great Hall protection spell.

### Preserve-vs-change guidance
Preserve:
- The state machine, main loop, canvas sizing, radial tap hit testing, random sequence generation, life loss, 10-coin reward, localStorage persistence, shop behavior, and audio trigger timing.
- The mobile-first single-tap input model.
- The one-screen memory challenge.

Change safely:
- Copy, titles, button text, HUD icons, theme names, color palettes, shop labels, and feedback labels.
- Canvas motifs, backgrounds, particles, glyph shapes, and CSS atmosphere.
- Approved remote audio/GIF/font mappings, if used.
- Conceptual five-level framing through presentation and only existing safe knobs (`sequenceLength`, `memorizeDuration`) when playtested.

Avoid:
- Adding movement, combat, physics, enemies, aiming, draggable objects, input timers, hidden controls, or shrinking tap targets.
- Rewriting core gameplay logic to force the theme.

## Five-level intended blueprint
1. **First-Year Wand Sparks** — base classroom spell-rune recall.
2. **Potion Pattern Lab** — same recall loop framed as stabilizing ingredient glows.
3. **Quidditch Signal Practice** — same loop framed as aerial team signal charms.
4. **Forbidden Forest Lumos Trail** — darker, higher-pressure recall to keep a trail lit.
5. **Great Hall Final Charm** — culminating castle protection sequence near the readable memory limit.

## Downstream priority
Later stages should implement the theme with procedural Canvas/CSS art first: castle silhouettes, floating candles, spell circles, wand sparks, potions bubbles, banners, forest wisps, and Great Hall star ceiling. Mechanics must remain intact.

The implemented game is a simple one-screen mobile relaxation arcade / toy collection. It is not a traditional fail-state game. It offers nine low-pressure micro-activities:

- In game: tap, hold, drag, or observe depending on the selected mode.

- CSS defines full-screen mobile layout, central panels, HUD cards, health strip, feedback GIF overlays, and responsive sizing.
- JavaScript defines an `AudioController`, configuration/state objects, input handlers, game logic, rendering functions, and start/restart UI bindings.
- Canvas rendering is procedural: background, player, enemies, projectiles, particles, and damage shake are drawn in code.
- Remote audio and GIF URLs are already referenced; this stage does not replace media.

### Game loop / state model
Screen states are start screen, active play with HUD, and game-over/restart screen. The start button primes audio, hides the start screen, shows HUD, initializes state, sets `gameActive`, and enters `requestAnimationFrame(gameLoop)`. The loop increments `frame`, spawns enemies, updates all entities, draws, and schedules itself until `gameActive` becomes false. Game over stops BGM, hides HUD, shows final score, and waits for restart.

### Player goals and interaction pattern
The player drags horizontally with mouse or touch to move a bottom-anchored character. Shooting is automatic. The goal is to destroy descending enemies for score while avoiding contact damage. Health starts at three hearts and reaches game over at zero.

### Core systems
- Horizontal target movement with lerp smoothing.
- Automatic projectile creation on cooldown.
- Score-scaled enemy spawning and enemy speed.
- Three enemy archetypes: 1 HP basic, 2 HP durable, and fast weaving.
- AABB projectile/enemy and enemy/player collision.
- Score HUD, health HUD, particles, damage flash, screen shake, and audio/GIF feedback.

### Inferred genre/gameplay shape
Medium arcade loop: simple controls but real-time timing, spatial positioning, target selection, and increasing pressure.

The Harry Potter remix should become **Hogwarts Spellstorm Defense**: a magical arcade defense game where a young wizard defender auto-casts spells upward while the player drags left/right to line up spell bolts against enchanted threats. # Blueprint — Remix v4 Inference Plus

## Current game reality

### High-level code structure
- `index.html` is a self-contained browser game.
- Rendering is implemented with Three.js imported from `./assets/unpkg.com/three_0.160.0/build/three.module.js`.
- CSS defines the HUD, start/pause/game-over screens, touch controls, feedback overlays, and mobile sizing.
- JavaScript modules inside `index.html` define:
  - `CFG` constants for grid, road size, colors, and world scale.
  - `STATE` for current screen, cash, timer, mission, car pose/speed, and input booleans.
  - `MEDIA`, `AUDIO`, and `FEEDBACK` for approved remote audio/GIF overlays already mapped in code.
  - `world` for procedural Manhattan-style grid generation.
  - `GPS` for A* route calculation and animated route ribbon rendering.
  - car mesh construction, beacon marker construction, physics, mission assignment, objective checking, camera follow, timer, and UI input binding.

### Genre / gameplay shape
The game is a simple-to-medium one-screen/mobile 3D arcade driving loop. The player drives a small taxi-like vehicle through a procedural grid city, follows a colored route beam to a pickup marker, stops close to the marker, then follows a second route beam to a drop-off marker. Successful drop-offs award cash while pickups/drop-offs refresh the countdown timer.

### Game loop / state model
1. Start screen explains the route objective.
2. Pressing `START SHIFT` resets score/time, spawns the vehicle on a road cell, creates the first mission, and enters play.
3. During play:
   - gas/brake/left/right input changes vehicle speed and heading;
   - grid collision blocks travel through buildings and bounces the vehicle back;
   - GPS route beams update from current grid cell to current target;
   - beacon marks the target;
   - stopping near the beacon completes pickup/dropoff;
   - dropoff adds cash;
   - every mission adds time up to the 60-second cap;
   - timer reaches zero and enters game over.
4. Pause screen can resume or restart.
5. Game-over screen displays final cash and allows retry.

### Player goals
- Primary goal: complete as many pickup/dropoff pairs as possible before time expires.
- Score state: `STATE.cash`, displayed as route credits, increases only after drop-off.
- Survival/progress pressure: timer counts down and is refreshed by completing mission steps.

### Interaction pattern / controls
- Mobile-first on-screen controls:
  - left/right steering buttons;
  - gas and brake pedals;
  - pause button.
- Pointer events are used for mobile/touch and mouse.
- Keyboard is only used to unlock audio; there is no keyboard driving implementation in the current source.
- The control model depends on analog-like hold duration and vehicle inertia.

### Camera / viewport assumptions
- Perspective follow camera behind the car.
- If the ideal camera position would be inside a non-road grid cell, it moves overhead.
- Canvas fills the viewport and HUD overlays absolute-positioned DOM controls.
- Mobile sizing is explicitly handled with viewport meta, safe-area padding, and responsive button sizes.

### Current presentation identity
The current presentation is a neon sky-cab / magic GPS taxi dispatch theme. It already contains some magical/futuristic wording and colored route beams, but it is not specifically Harry Potter-themed. The 3D world is an abstract neon Manhattan grid with colorful block buildings.

## Intended remixed trajectory: Harry Potter

The remix should become a magical school/witchcraft-world courier run while preserving every core driving mechanic. The player pilots an enchanted flying/rolling cab or broom-car through a procedurally generated wizarding campus/castle-road grid, follows spell-guidance ribbons to find students, owl post, potion parcels, or magical checkpoints, then completes drop-offs before the shift timer expires.

The Harry Potter direction should be achieved through:
- wording: shift, cash, pickup, dropoff become wizard courier, house points, summons, deliveries;
- visual styling: castle towers, house banners, floating candles, owls, spell sparks, parchment panels;
- vehicle mesh: same collision body, but visually reads as an enchanted Ford Anglia / broom-cab silhouette;
- route beams: blue/orange become charm trails, patronus-like ribbons, or spell navigation beams;
- beacons: mission target becomes a glowing spell circle, owl perch, potion crate, student silhouette, or house crest marker;
- buildings: blocks become castle towers, greenhouses, Quidditch stands, library stacks, Hogsmeade roofs, forbidden forest silhouettes;
- UI/HUD: credits become house points, timer becomes curfew bell / shift clock;
- audio: use approved catalog mystical/dungeon/village audio if later stages replace current audio.

## Preserve-vs-change guidance

### Preserve
- The Three.js render loop architecture.
- `STATE.screen` flow: start, play, pause, over.
- Timer semantics: countdown during play, game over at zero.
- Score semantics: score/cash increases after drop-off only.
- Mission alternation: pickup then dropoff.
- Control semantics: gas, brake, left, right, pause/resume/restart/retry.
- Vehicle inertia, turn behavior, speed caps, collision response, and stop-near-target objective check.
- Grid-road navigation and A* GPS route planning.
- Mobile-safe DOM controls and pointer event input.

### Change safely
- Text labels and mission copy.
- CSS colors, fonts from approved catalog, parchment/glow/house styling.
- Three.js material colors and small additive mesh decorations.
- Building colors/shapes if done without changing road grid/collision semantics.
- Beacon and route material colors/effects.
- Noninteractive background and atmospheric particles.
- HUD labels, start/pause/game-over copy.
- Approved remote media URL mapping from catalogs.

### Do not change in this stage or downstream without a tiny documented repair reason
- Collision model.
- World grid road/building logic.
- A* pathfinding rules.
- Movement physics.
- Timer/score/win-loss semantics.
- Input event semantics.
- Main loop structure.
- Canvas/HUD layering in a way that could block controls.
